cs.t: My dream computer was a Fujitsu Stylistic ST-4110 w/ a Wacom stylus which I carried everywhere (along w/ a spare battery), and I had docking stations for it at home, and at work, along w/ power supplies, so that I just dropped it in place and used it w/ an external keyboard and mouse. When mobile, it had a transflective display which allowed me to use it in full, bright, direct sunlight, so I used it as an ebook reader, and map reader (w/ a USB GPS). I despair of replacing it --- these days I have: - a Samsung Galaxy Book 12 --- very nice machine, but the OLED washes out in bright sunlight, and I have to keep the drive full so that it won't update beyond Windows 10 build 1703 (Fall Creators Update breaks the stylus so that it won't select text, or draw in older apps such as Freehand) - Galaxy Note 10+ --- wonderfully portable, I carry it places that the Fujitsu never would have gone, but again, the display doesn't work in the sun - Kindle Scribe --- screen works great in sunlight, and it uses the same stylus technology as my other devices, so excellent synergy, but loading maps is a pain, and there's no GPS - a Wacom One connected to my MacBook at my desk I desperately want a computer which: - has a daylight viewable display (this idea that one can out-bright the sun on a battery-powered device is just idiocy) - has a nice stylus (Wacom EMR, the current generation is fine --- I suppose my next computer will be a Wacom Cintiq Companion, but that will use a different stylus tec

I really miss, and worry that I will never be able to replace my Fujitsu Stylistic ST-4110 which had a transflective display (which allowed using it in full-bright, direct sunlight, even at the beach) and a stylus --- closest I came was a Samsung Galaxy Book 12 (which I wasn't able to replace). The problem is, trying to out-bright the sun on a battery-powered device is exactly as stupid as it sounds, and solutions such as transflective displays don't showroom well (someone should build a showroom w/ a light booth which simulates a bright sunny day and invite folks to try to use devices in it w/o shading them). At this point in time, I'm seriously considering switching to a Raspberry Pi 5 as a daily driver (paired w/ a Wacom One 13 gen2 display w/ touch) --- if that display could be supplemented by (or swapped out for) an e-ink or similar daylight viewable pen-enabled display, it would probably push me over the edge (and yes, I've considered just pointing my Kindle Scribe's web browser at a page on the rPi --- if someone has a tool which would allow this to capture stylus input, please let me know).
cs.th: E Ink faces growing competition in the "paper-like" display space
